newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish public debt fell to 70 pct of GDP in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Danish public debt fell to 70 pct of GDP in 1996.

text.p: Danish net government debt was 599 billion crowns ($94 billion) at the end of 1996, or 59 percent of gross domestic product, up from 578 billion in 1995 but down as a percentage of GDP from 60 percent, a central bank report said on Wednesday.
Overall public debt, including local authorities and public institutions, fell to 70 percent of GDP in 1996 from 72 percent the year before, the bank said.
EU criteria for economic and monetary union state that a nation's gross government debt should be 60 percent of GDP or approaching that level at a "satisfactory pace."
A 1993 referendum allows Denmark to opt out of EMU. A reversal of that decision requires a fresh plebiscite, for which the government says it so far has no plans.
The central bank report said foreign investors raised their holdings of Danish government bonds to 35 percent of the total in 1996 from 32 percent in 1995.
The government sold securities to a nominal value of 97.576 billion crowns in 1996, of which 84.927 billion were bonds of maturities ranging from 1999 to 2024.
It placed 19.8 billion in treasury bills of up to three-years maturity and logged a debit of 7.151 billion for conversion of short-dated treasury notes, it said.
